# ETL templates drift allowlist (S8-5, #384)
#
# One substring per non-blank, non-comment line. Failure lines reported by
# `scripts/check_etl_templates.py` that contain ANY listed substring are
# tolerated; everything else fails the CI guardrail.
#
# Failure lines emitted by the driver have one of the shapes:
#   "  drift <template-path>: <reason>"          (Pydantic parse failure)
#   "  drift <sample-path>: <reason>"            (sample command failure)
#
# CONVENTION: every entry MUST be accompanied by a comment immediately
# above it explaining (a) which template + check it covers and (b) why
# the failure is irreducible (link to an ADR / changelog entry / sprint
# story). Adding a bare substring with no rationale is a review-block.
#
# A second escape hatch is available for in-line per-template suppression:
# add the following comment as the FIRST line of the template YAML to skip
# both the Pydantic parse and the sample run for that template:
#
#   # valdo-drift-allowed: <one-line justification>
#
# Use the inline form when the template itself is the carve-out (e.g. a
# legitimate WIP scaffolding template living under templates/etl/). Use
# this allowlist file when the failure surface is a known engine quirk
# that crosses multiple templates.
#
# To remove an entry: ensure the underlying failure has actually been
# fixed, run `scripts/check_etl_templates.sh` locally, and only then
# delete the line.

# (no allowlist entries yet -- every committed template under
# templates/etl/ parses cleanly through SourceConfig and either ships a
# build_sample.py that exits 0 or a left.csv/right.csv pair that `valdo
# compare` round-trips with exit 0.)
